Introduction:

Mendocino County Superior Court is a city courthouse serving the residents of Mendocino County, California. It is located within the court of appeal in the first district, and the request from the northern state district goes to the ninth circuit United State Court of appeal. The courthouse was established in 1859; it was replaced with a new building in 1872. A new courthouse with a new annex and modern technologies was built in 1956 and is serving the county's people nowadays. The court's mission is to resolve fights and provide justice to everyone. It has jurisdiction over criminal, small claims, probation, juvenile, appeal, civil, family, traffic, and vehicle matters. They provide online services like online payment, forms, fines, record searching, and many more, so it is optional to go to court for these services. This court also provides self-help for a different division. Proper dressing is required during the court session, and wearing a mask is mandatory. Three superior courts located in this county are:

  • MENDOCINO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – ARENA BRANCH
  • MENDOCINO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – TEN MILE BRANCH
  • MENDOCINO COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – UKIAH COURTHOUSE
Different courts of Mendocino

How to search for case information?

Mendocino County Court Case Search can be done online using the court online case search portal https://portal-camendocino.tylertech.cloud/Portal/. All the records are maintained by the court online or in a database. The search can be done in the following ways:

  • Search by record or case number
  • Search by First, Middle and Last name

After entering the data, the information will display. If the information does not come, the case records will be confidential and cannot be displayed online. You have to go to the court and give a request for these types of documents, and then the court will decide whether to provide that information to you or not.

How to search for a case hearing?

Mendocino County Court case hearings can be searched through the court portal. Type the location, hearing types, date and search types. The search types can be done in the following ways:

  • Search by Case Number
  • Search by Party Name
  • Search by Business Name
  • Search by Attorney Name
  • Search by Attorney Bar Number
  • Search by Judicial Officer
  • Search by Courtroom

How to make a payment?

Mendocino County Court payment can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, US funds, or a card at the court payment office. Take your ticket and case number with you when you come for payment. 2% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

Online

Online payments can be made using the Court portal https://portal-camendocino.tylertech.cloud/Portal/. Search your case by entering any search type, like a case number, name, party name etc., with the criteria. Your case information with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Select the payment option and pay the amount online. Convenience fees will be applied using this method. You can also use this method for installments and a 30-day extension of appearance or fine payment.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address, 00 North State Street. Ukiah, CA 95482. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number, and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

How to appear remotely?

Mendocino County Court remote appearances for some eligible cases are possible using telephone and video conferencing in the zoom application. Fill out and send the form related to your case. The court will respond with a schedule and a meeting link ID for video conferencing or telephonic hearing if your case is eligible for the remote hearing. Make sure your internet connection is strong. Mute your microphone and speak only when the judge calls your name. Test your microphone and video before joining the session. It is recommended to avoid running unnecessary applications when you are in a meeting. Wear a proper dress and sit where your face is visible. Recording for the case hearing is not allowed. If your presence is disruptive to the court proceedings, then the court has the right to cancel the zoom hearing.

The family court division handles which types of cases?

Mendocino County family court division handles cases related to family issues and matters. These issues include divorce, nullity, legal separation, child custody, visitation and support, adoption, domestic violence etc. This division also provides family mediation self-help services that give child custody recommending counseling, guidance to divorce and legal separation and probate conservatorship that appoints judges to investigate new and continuing conservatorship.

The traffic court handles which types of cases?

Mendocino County traffic court handles adult traffic and vehicle violations that include speeding, driving without or with an expired license, going while you have drugs, accidents etc. The court will mail you a courtesy notice on the citation address after you receive a traffic or infraction ticket. That notice will give detailed information on the fine amount, deadline and many more. If your citation includes a court appearance, then appearing in the court on the schedule is mandatory. Many options for resolving traffic tickets if a court appearance is not required are:

  • Sign up for the traffic school if your case is eligible for it. After completing it, your traffic infraction records will be removed.
  • Pay the total amount of the fine on time.
  • Reduce your fine by Correcting the mechanical violations like headlight, mirrors etc.
  • If you cannot pay the fine on time, seek a reduction in the fine from the court.
  • You can request community service if you do not want to pay a fine.
  • Enter a plea of not guilty and request a court trial.

You had to respond with a solution before the deadline. Contact the clerk's office if you are still waiting to receive any mail for courtesy notice.

How many types of juvenile cases are handled by this court?

Mendocino County juvenile court handles the cases in which a minor is involved. Two types of cases are taken that are:

Juvenile delinquency cases

It includes cases in which a juvenile violates the rules and is charged with violating the law, and it is considered a crime if an adult commits it. Delinquency matters will be set on department G at 1:30 pm on Tuesday and Thursday.

Juvenile dependency cases

It involves a case in which the juvenile is neglected or abused. The dependency matters will be set on department G at 9:00 pm from Tuesday to Thursday.

Juvenile cases are confidential, and the data is only provided to the person involved when they request by coming to the court. Juvenile case filing fees are free.

How can small claims cases be filled?

Mendocino County small division handles all the matters in which the claim is up to $10,000. The small claim case can be filled out by filling out the form on the website or by visiting the court in person. Enter your and the defendant's personal information, the amount you want to claim with a reason. After filing the case, prepare for your court date. You can take legal advice from an attorney or lawyer, but the clerk cannot provide legal advice. The night court is also available after 5:30, but only if someone requests it for a valid reason.

Which types of collaborative programs do this court offer?

Mendocino County collaborative programs focus on criminal defendant assistance and assist parents with children in the foster care system with mental health issues or addiction. Three types of joint programs are offered by this court that are:

  • Adult Drug Court
  • Behavioral Health Court
  • Family Dependency Drug Court

What are the steps for changing an adult's name?

Mendocino County self-help provides the facility for the name change for adults 18+. Some basic steps that must be followed during this name change are:

  • File the form online or by visiting the court
  • You had to publish the form in an approved newspaper
  • After it, you receive a court order that the judge signs
  • Change your legal documents after all the steps are done

You can take help from the link if you need help or guidance https://california.tylerhost.net/SRL/SRL/Start?legalProcessKey=Petition_for_Change_of_Name.

FAQ:

How can I check my juror status?

You can check your juror status by https://jury.mendocino.courts.ca.gov/ . Enter the juror ID number with your date of birth.

How much time is taken for the finalization of divorce?

When you file for divorce and submit all the documents then after 6 months the divorce will be finalized.
